parentNote.en: Every question is answered in the app. Each goal has a short home activity: say the words aloud together, and let your child guess first.
parentNote.ar: كل الأسئلة الطفل بيحلها جوه البرنامج، ولكل هدف نشاط قصير في البيت. قولوا الكلمات بصوت عالي مع بعض، وسيبوا طفلك يتوقع الأول.

steps.title: Story time: Tiddalik the Thirsty Frog
steps.prompt: Tap each part of the story to listen.

options.label: Beginning. Long ago, Tiddalik the frog was so thirsty that he drank all the water in the land.
Middle. The animals tried to make him laugh. Kangaroo boxed his own shadow. Thump, thump!
End. Platypus woke up so cross that he looked silly. Tiddalik laughed, and all the water gushed out.

steps.explanation: A traditional tale is a very old story told again and again. Many teach a lesson.
steps.shortExplanation: A traditional tale is a very old story told again and again. Many teach a lesson.

englishVisual.title: Tiddalik the Thirsty Frog
englishVisual.text: An old story from Australia. The lesson: share.

steps.title: More old tales

options.label: The Lion and the Mouse. A little mouse nibbles through the hunters' ropes and sets the lion free. Small can be strong too.
The Ungrateful Tiger. A kind man helps Tiger out of a trap, but Tiger wants to eat him! Clever Rabbit tricks Tiger back in.
The King of the Forest. Tiger King saves Lion from the waterfall, and they live in peace. Be kind.

steps.explanation: Many traditional tales have animal characters and a lesson hiding inside.
steps.shortExplanation: Many traditional tales have animal characters and a lesson hiding inside.

steps.title: Every sentence needs a verb

options.label: Many old tales start with Once upon a time, or Long ago.
Every sentence needs a doing word, a verb. The frog drank the water.
And joins two ideas: Tiger is hungry and cross.

steps.explanation: Every sentence needs a verb, and and joins two ideas together.
steps.shortExplanation: Every sentence needs a verb, and and joins two ideas together.

steps.title: Join with and
steps.prompt: Tiger is hungry. Tiger is cross. Which one joins them with and?
steps.hint: And goes between the two things Tiger is.
steps.explanation: Tiger is hungry and cross. And joins the two ideas.
steps.shortExplanation: Tiger is hungry and cross. And joins the two ideas.

steps.title: Is there a verb?
steps.prompt: Does each sentence have a verb?
steps.hint: Ask: what did it do? If nothing is done, the verb is missing.
steps.explanation: Drank and boxed are verbs. The other two sentences have no doing word.
steps.shortExplanation: Drank and boxed are verbs. The other two sentences have no doing word.

source.answerKeyText: a ✓ • b ✗ (no verb) • c ✓ • d ✗ (no verb)

steps.title: Who did what?
steps.prompt: Match each animal to what it did.
steps.hint: Remember the story: who was thirsty, and who woke up cross?
steps.explanation: Tiddalik drank the water, Kookaburra told jokes, Kangaroo boxed and Platypus got cross.
steps.shortExplanation: Tiddalik drank the water, Kookaburra told jokes, Kangaroo boxed and Platypus got cross.

source.answerKeyText: Tiddalik – drank all the water • Kookaburra – told jokes • Kangaroo – boxed his shadow • Platypus – got cross and looked silly

steps.title: How did he feel?
steps.prompt: How did the man feel when Tiger grabbed him?
steps.hint: Tiger wanted to eat him! Show me that face.
steps.explanation: Tiger wanted to eat him, so the man felt scared.
steps.shortExplanation: Tiger wanted to eat him, so the man felt scared.

source.answerKeyText: Scared / frightened ("surprised" or "sad" show good thinking too)

steps.title: Who tricked Tiger?
steps.prompt: Who tricked Tiger back into the trap?
steps.hint: It was a clever animal in The Ungrateful Tiger.
steps.explanation: Clever Rabbit asked Tiger to show him, and Tiger jumped back into the trap.
steps.shortExplanation: Clever Rabbit asked Tiger to show him, and Tiger jumped back into the trap.

steps.title: A story opener
steps.prompt: …, there was a thirsty frog. Which story opener fits?
steps.hint: How do old stories often start?
steps.explanation: Once upon a time is a story opener. It starts a story.
steps.shortExplanation: Once upon a time is a story opener. It starts a story.

source.answerKeyText: Any opener: Once upon a time, Long ago, Long, long ago, One day

steps.title: Super verbs
steps.prompt: The lion roared. The water gushed. The cat pounced. Tap the three verbs.
steps.hint: Look for the words ending in ed.
steps.explanation: Roared, gushed and pounced are the verbs. They all end in ed.
steps.shortExplanation: Roared, gushed and pounced are the verbs. They all end in ed.

source.answerKeyText: a roared • b gushed • c pounced

steps.title: Tiddalik's lesson
steps.prompt: What lesson does Tiddalik the Thirsty Frog teach us?
steps.hint: What went wrong when Tiddalik kept all the water?
steps.explanation: Tiddalik kept all the water for himself. The story teaches us to share.
steps.shortExplanation: Tiddalik kept all the water for himself. The story teaches us to share.

source.answerKeyText: A good answer says we should share and not keep everything for ourselves.

steps.title: What is a traditional tale?

options.label: very old stories told again and again

steps.hint: Grandmas and grandpas told them long ago.
steps.explanation: Traditional tales are very old stories that people told again and again.
steps.shortExplanation: Traditional tales are very old stories that people told again and again.

source.answerKeyText: very old stories told again and again

steps.title: Once upon a time
steps.prompt: Once upon a time is a…
steps.hint: Where in a story do you hear it?
steps.explanation: Once upon a time is a story opener. It starts a story.
steps.shortExplanation: Once upon a time is a story opener. It starts a story.

steps.title: Why did Tiddalik laugh?
steps.explanation: Platypus was so cross that he looked silly, and Tiddalik laughed.
steps.shortExplanation: Platypus was so cross that he looked silly, and Tiddalik laughed.

steps.title: Who saved the lion?
steps.prompt: In the lion story, the lion was saved by…
steps.explanation: The little mouse nibbled through the ropes. Small can be strong too.
steps.shortExplanation: The little mouse nibbled through the ropes. Small can be strong too.

steps.title: A sentence with a verb
steps.prompt: Which one is a sentence with a verb?
steps.hint: Which one tells us what the frog did?
steps.explanation: Jumped is a doing word, so The frog jumped is a sentence.
steps.shortExplanation: Jumped is a doing word, so The frog jumped is a sentence.

stickers.meaning: A very old story told again and again.

goalActivities.text: Play the and game: you say a short sentence, like "The lion is big", and your child makes it longer with and.
goalActivities.textAr: العبوا لعبة and: تقول جملة قصيرة زي "The lion is big"، وطفلك يطوّلها بـ and.

goalActivities.textAr: مثّلوا قصة Tiddalik مع بعض: واحد يبقى الضفدعة، والتاني يمثّل كل حيوان بيحاول يضحّكه.

goalActivities.text: Stand at a mirror and make faces for happy, sad, cross and scared. Ask: how did the man feel when Tiger grabbed him? Show me.
goalActivities.textAr: قفوا قدام المراية واعملوا وشوش: مبسوط، زعلان، متضايق، خايف. واسأل: الراجل حس بإيه لما النمر مسكه؟ ورّيني.

goalActivities.text: Ask: was it right to trick Tiger? Is it ever right to trick someone? Let your child explain their idea.
goalActivities.textAr: اسأل: كان صح إنهم يضحكوا على النمر؟ ينفع نضحك على حد؟ وسيب طفلك يشرح رأيه.
